speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you're experiencing fatigue and severe itching; can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, and have you had any recent changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to rule out primary sclerosing cholangitis, so I will request an MRCP and liver biopsy. I will also order hepatitis B and C serologies to exclude viral causes given your sexual history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now request the results of the MRCP, liver biopsy, and hepatitis serologies to determine the underlying cause of your liver dysfunction. REQUEST TEST: MRCP REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_C_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP and hepatitis serologies effectively rule out primary sclerosing cholangitis and viral hepatitis, which is unexpected given your history. Do you have any personal or family history of autoimmune diseases, and have you noticed any darkening of the urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, I am shifting focus to autoimmune causes like Primary Biliary Cholangitis. I will request an Antimitochondrial Antibody (AMA) test and a comprehensive metabolic panel to assess bilirubin levels. speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated alkaline phosphatase with negative AMA suggests an autoimmune cholangiopathy other than PBC, possibly IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis or autoimmune hepatitis overlap. I will request IgG4 levels and an autoimmune hepatitis panel to further narrow the differential. REQUEST TEST: IgG4_level REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative AMA, normal IgG4, and normal autoimmune hepatitis panel, I am considering primary sclerosing cholangitis with normal MRCP or drug-induced liver injury. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests_Request REQUEST IMAGES

text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation strongly suggest Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, despite the initially normal MRCP. I will now confirm the diagnosis with a more sensitive magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography focused on small duct disease. REQUEST TEST: MRCP_with_small_duct_protocol

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal MRCP and negative autoimmune markers, the ultrasound shows bile duct thickening and you have a history of ulcerative colitis, which strongly points to small-duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. I will request a liver biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the strong association with ulcerative colitis, cholestatic liver enzymes, and characteristic bile duct changes on ultrasound despite a normal MRCP and non-diagnostic biopsy, the clinical picture is most consistent with small-duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Small-duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
